## Associative · Change the grouping {#fv1-associative .fv-lesson }

```{=html}
<p>An operation is <strong>associative</strong> when changing the grouping does not change the result.</p><div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="\displaystyle (\textcolor{#80579a}{2}\times\textcolor{#217864}{3})\times\textcolor{#ad6e32}{4}=\textcolor{#80579a}{2}\times(\textcolor{#217864}{3}\times\textcolor{#ad6e32}{4})"></span></div><div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="\displaystyle 6\times\textcolor{#ad6e32}{4}=\textcolor{#80579a}{2}\times12=24"></span></div><div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="\displaystyle \textcolor{#80579a}{m}(\textcolor{#217864}{a}\textcolor{#ad6e32}{b})=(\textcolor{#80579a}{m}\textcolor{#217864}{a})\textcolor{#ad6e32}{b}=\textcolor{#217864}{a}(\textcolor{#80579a}{m}\textcolor{#ad6e32}{b})"></span></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §1.1 · p. 1</div>

::: {.notes}
About one minute. The colours track the unchanged factors 2, 3 and 4 as the brackets move. Pure associativity is m(ab)=(ma)b. The final form a(mb) also uses commutativity of real multiplication. Connect this to moving one scalar factor in the vector rule; do not add a three-vector dot-product discussion. The calculation and identities are all visible immediately.
:::
